'''Kenji Fukaya''' (Japanese: 深谷賢治, ''Fukaya Kenji'', born in 1959<ref>{{Cite web| title=The Shaw Prize - Press Conference | date=2025-05-27 | url=https://www.shawprize.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2025-Press-Kit_Eng_250527.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250527144841/https://www.shawprize.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2025-Press-Kit_Eng_250527.pdf | archive-date=2025-05-27}}</ref>) is a Japanese mathematician known for his  work in [[symplectic geometry]] and  [[Riemannian geometry]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scgp.stonybrook.edu/people/faculty/bios/kenji-fukaya |title=Kenji Fukaya &#124; SCGP |publisher=Scgp.stonybrook.edu |date=2013-04-01 |access-date=2013-10-14}}</ref> His many fundamental contributions to mathematics include the discovery of the [[Fukaya category]]. He was a permanent faculty member at the [[Simons Center for Geometry and Physics]] and a professor of mathematics at [[Stony Brook University]] before leaving for [[Tsinghua University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-19 |title=Respected mathematician Kenji Fukaya leaves US for China's Tsinghua University |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3279101/respected-mathematician-kenji-fukaya-leaves-us-teach-chinas-tsinghua-university |access-date=2024-09-19 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==
[[File:Fukaya seidel.jpg|thumb|Kenji Fukaya (left) with [[Paul Seidel]], [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach]] 2002]]
Fukaya was both an undergraduate and a graduate student in mathematics at the [[University of Tokyo]], receiving  his BA in 1981, and his PhD  in 1986. In 1987, he joined the University of Tokyo faculty as an associate professor. He then moved to [[Kyoto University]] as a full professor in 1994. In 2013, he then moved to the United States in order to join the faculty of the [[Simons Center for Geometry and Physics]] at Stony Brook.{{Citation needed|date=June 2025}}

The [[Fukaya category]], meaning the <math>A_\infty</math> category of whose objects are Lagrangian submanifolds of a given [[symplectic manifold]], is named after him, and is intimately related to [[Floer homology]]. Other contributions to symplectic geometry include his proof (with [[Kaoru Ono]]) of a weak version of the [[Arnold conjecture]] and a construction of general [[Gromov–Witten invariants]]. His many other mathematical contributions include important theorems in Riemannian geometry and work on physics-related topics such as gauge theory and mirror symmetry.{{Citation needed|date=June 2025}}

Fukaya was awarded the [[Mathematical Society of Japan|Japanese Mathematical Society's]] [[Geometry Prize]] in 1989<ref>{{cite web | url=http://geom.math.se.tmu.ac.jp/en/prize-e.html | title=Mathematical Society of Japan Geometry Section Web Site | access-date=2021-12-21 | archive-date=2022-11-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221119203129/http://geom.math.se.tmu.ac.jp/en/prize-e.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> and [[Spring Prize]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Spring_Prize/ | title=Spring Prize of the Mathematical Society of Japan|website=Mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk }}</ref> He also received the [[Inoue Prize]] in 2002, the [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] in 2003,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.japan-acad.go.jp/en/activities/jyusho/091to100.html | title=The Imperial Prize, Japan Academy Prize, Duke of Edinburgh Prize Recipients 91st - 100th|website=Japan-acad.go.jp}}</ref>  the [[Asahi Prize]] in 2009,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.asahi.com/corporate/award/asahi/12737983 | title=THE ASAHI PRIZE (English version) &#124; 朝日新聞社の会社案内|website=Asahi.com }}</ref> and the [[Fujihara Award]] in 2012.<ref>[https://133.125.34.249/en/publicity/news20121001-en.html] {{Dead link|date=December 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He has served on the governing board of the Japanese Mathematical Society and on the Mathematical Committee of the Science Council of Japan. In 2025 he was awarded the [[Shaw Prize]] in Mathematics.<ref name="Shaw Prize 2025">{{Cite web|url=https://www.shawprize.org/news/announcement-press-conference-2025-press-release/|title=Announcement Press Conference 2025 Press Release|website=Shawprize.org|access-date=August 20, 2026}}</ref>

Fukaya was an invited speaker at the 1990 International Congress of Mathematicians in Kyoto, where he gave a talk entitled, ''Collapsing Riemannian Manifolds and its Applications.''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=&order=field_speakers_congress_city&sort=desc&page=101 | title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers |website=Mathunion.org}}</ref>
